note: The marketing matrix (EE-062): who a venture's public site speaks to, what each audience needs to learn, and how prominent each piece of information must be. Version 0.x, ours and unevaluated: where information belongs varies by startup type, product and industry, and this is a starting opinion to replace with researched practice. Every item is public by default (publish: true), and each names the record it comes from.

customers.label: Customers
customers.why: every venture sells to someone; the ICPs in purpose/icp are this audience

investors.label: Investors
investors.why: only a priority while the venture is raising

talent.label: Candidates
talent.why: only a priority while the venture is hiring

contributors.label: Contributors and community
contributors.why: only when the venture invites contributors (open source, community, creators)

partners.label: Partners
partners.why: integrations, channels and resellers find the venture through the site

press.label: Press
press.why: journalists look for the story, the team and a contact

facts.raising: the venture is raising capital or wants investors to reach out
facts.hiring: the venture is hiring or wants candidates to reach out
facts.contributors: the venture invites contributors: open source, community, creators or volunteers

nav.means: in the home page's header or navigation

linked.means: linked from the home page (the footer will do)

what.label: What it is, in one line
what.question: what the venture or product is, in a sentence or two

why.investors: investors decide in one line whether to read further
why.talent: candidates need to know what they would work on
why.contributors: contributors need to know what they would help build
why.partners: partners need to know what they would integrate with or resell

who-for.label: Who it is for
who-for.question: who the product is for: the kind of customer, user or business it serves

why.investors: investors look for a clear, reachable market
why.partners: partners check whether the customers overlap with theirs

problem.label: The problem it solves
problem.question: the problem or pain the product solves

why.investors: investors back a painful problem before a product

how.label: How it works
how.question: how the product works or what it does, step by step or feature by feature

why.partners: partners need to see where they would fit

proof.label: Proof
proof.question: proof that it works: customers, testimonials, logos, results or numbers

why.investors: traction is what investors look for first

pricing.label: Pricing
pricing.question: what it costs: prices, plans or how pricing works

next-step.label: A clear next step
next-step.question: a clear next step for a visitor: sign up, start free, book a demo, join a waitlist or buy

team.label: Who is behind it
team.question: who founded or runs the venture: the founders or team by name

why.investors: early-stage investors back the team as much as the idea
why.talent: candidates want to know who they would work with

mission.label: Mission and vision
mission.question: why the venture exists: its mission, vision or story

why.talent: candidates choose ventures whose mission they share
why.investors: investors look for founders with a long-run ambition
why.press: the mission is often the story's angle
why.contributors: contributors give time to missions they share

contact.label: How to reach them
contact.question: how to contact the venture: an email, a form or a contact page

why.partners: partners need a person to start a conversation with
why.investors: investors need a way to reach the founders

hiring.label: Whether they are hiring
hiring.question: whether the venture is hiring, with open roles or how to apply

why.talent: candidates look for open roles and how to apply

raising.label: Information for investors
raising.question: information for investors: that the venture is raising, its backers, or how investors can reach it

why.investors: investors need to know the venture is raising and how to reach it

contribute.label: How to contribute
contribute.question: how someone can contribute or join the community: open source, a community, volunteering or creating

why.contributors: contributors need to know how to start

press.label: News and press
press.question: news, press coverage, announcements or a press kit

why.press: journalists look for news and a press kit

trust.label: Trust and privacy
trust.question: how the venture protects data and privacy, or the security and compliance it meets

why.partners: partners check that the venture handles shared data responsibly

customer_types.note: What a customer looks for on a site depends on who the customer is. Jev places the venture's ICP into one or more of these types; each type says how much each item matters to it and why. The reasons are ours, version 0.x and unevaluated: each is a claim to test with the venture's own customers, not a finding. Jev answers conservatively, so a type counts when its probability is at least 0.25 and at least 0.6 of the strongest type's.

what: every visitor has to learn what it is before anything else
who-for: visitors decide in seconds whether it is for them
problem: buyers recognise themselves in the problem before the product
how: buyers want to see how it would work for them
proof: buyers look for others like them who use it
pricing: most buyers check the price before they talk to anyone
next-step: a visitor who is convinced needs one obvious thing to do
team: most buyers judge the product, not the people behind it
mission: few buyers read the mission before buying
contact: some buyers want a person to ask
trust: buyers handing over data look for how it is protected

consumer.label: Consumers
consumer.about: individuals buying for themselves or their household

team: consumers buy the product; they rarely look up who founded it
proof: consumers lean on reviews and ratings from people like them
pricing: consumers compare prices before anything else
contact: consumers expect self-serve help more than a contact
mission: some consumers choose brands for what they stand for

smb-owner.label: Small-business owners
smb-owner.about: owners or operators of a small business buying for it, often alone and on their own money

team: owners spending their own money often want to see the people they are trusting
pricing: owners buy on a budget and leave if the price is hidden
proof: owners look for businesses like theirs that already use it
contact: owners want to reach a person before they commit

business-team.label: Teams inside companies
business-team.about: teams in a company (product, engineering, sales, marketing, operations) choosing a tool for their own work

how: teams want to see the workflow before they ask colleagues to switch
team: teams judge a tool by trying it, rarely by its founders
proof: teams look for companies like theirs already using it
pricing: per-seat pricing decides whether a team can adopt it without approval
trust: company data in the tool brings an IT or security check

business-team.match: teams|team of|product team|sales team|marketing team|ops team|workspace|collaborat

enterprise-buyer.label: Enterprise buyers
enterprise-buyer.about: managers or procurement teams buying for a larger organisation, with review and security sign-off

team: vendor-risk reviews ask who stands behind a vendor and whether it will last
trust: security and compliance review gates the purchase
proof: buyers need logos and case studies to justify the choice internally
pricing: enterprise prices are negotiated; a contact-sales path is expected
contact: enterprise buying runs through a sales conversation

developer.label: Developers
developer.about: engineers choosing a tool, library or API

how: developers want docs and examples before anything else
team: developers judge the docs and the code more than the founders
proof: developers look for adoption: stars, users, companies
pricing: developers check free tiers and usage pricing up front
next-step: developers want to try it immediately: sign up, install or an API key

regulated-professional.label: Regulated professionals
regulated-professional.about: clinicians, financial or legal professionals whose work carries patient, client or legal obligations

trust: they are liable for their clients' data, so privacy and compliance come first
team: they want to know the people handling their clients' data understand the field
proof: they trust peers in their own profession
contact: they want someone to answer compliance questions

creator.label: Creators and freelancers
creator.about: independent creators, freelancers and solo professionals

team: creators often follow the people behind a tool
mission: creators choose tools whose values match theirs
proof: creators follow other creators who use it

team: procurement asks who the vendor is and checks its standing
mission: mission fit matters to mission-driven buyers
trust: public data rules and accessibility requirements gate the purchase
contact: procurement runs through a named contact
